## 7. Developer checks and optional controls {#developer-boundaries}

Inspect the **actual target and emitted instruction sequence** in this order:

1. **Target and pipeline:** match the processor, compiler revision, function attributes and options to the [target scope](#llvm-wmma-handling) and [reviewed pass pipeline](#llvm-pass-pipeline).
2. **Register overlap and spacing:** identify physical D → A/B overlap and, on RDNA 4, the sparse-index input; inspect the intervening VALU or inserted vector no-op. Check D → C stall conditions separately. [Overlap handling](#llvm-wmma-spacing) · [C-only handling](#llvm-wmma-c-only).
3. **Memory readiness:** identify the operand's producer, pending dependencies and emitted wait counters. A memory-counter wait does not supply the WMMA register separator. [Operand readiness](#llvm-memory-readiness) · [Counter selection](#llvm-memory-counters).
4. **Inline assembly:** check the exposed register operands and the internal instruction sequence; do not assume LLVM repairs dependencies hidden inside the string. [Coverage boundary](#llvm-inline-asm).
5. **Optional controls:** check [ALU-delay eligibility](#llvm-alu-delay) and whether supported [GFX12 expert scheduling](#expert-scheduling) is enabled. Absence of an optional delay does not remove mandatory spacing or establish zero-stall execution.

### Inline assembly {#llvm-inline-asm .compiler-case}

```{=html}
<dl class="rule-details">
<div><dt>Compiler handling</dt><dd><p><strong>WMMA fix:</strong> requires recognized WMMA/SWMMAC opcodes; its backward scan skips inline assembly.</p><p><strong>Other handling:</strong> the dedicated inline-assembly checker limits its coverage; wait insertion analyzes modeled register operands and events.</p></dd></div>
<div><dt>Boundary</dt><dd><p>These paths do not establish automatic repair of dependencies hidden inside an assembly string.</p><p>Checking exposed operands is distinct from analyzing internal instructions. The ISA rules inside the string remain unchanged.</p></dd></div>
</dl>
```

### Optional S\_DELAY\_ALU and C reuse {#llvm-alu-delay .compiler-case}

```{=html}
<dl class="rule-details">
<div><dt>Pass eligibility</dt><dd><p>Requires <code>hasDelayAlu()</code>; skips functions with a maximum of one wave per execution unit.</p></dd></div>
<div><dt>C-reuse calculation</dt><dd><p>Excludes a tied explicit source equal to the remembered preceding WMMA/SWMMAC destination from delay calculation.</p><p><strong>Predicate:</strong> register equality and current instruction class; no opcode-type or SRC2-modifier comparison.</p></dd></div>
<div><dt>Tracking</dt><dd><p>Another processed instruction that is neither WMMA nor SWMMAC clears the remembered destination.</p></dd></div>
<div><dt>Hardware boundary</dt><dd><p><strong>Meaning:</strong> an optional compiler delay calculation, not a broader hardware-forwarding guarantee.</p><p>Neither the exclusion nor absence of <code>S_DELAY_ALU</code> removes mandatory WMMA spacing or ISA D → C stall conditions.</p></dd></div>
</dl>
```

### GFX12 expert-scheduling exception {#expert-scheduling}

:::: {.reading-block}

::: {.note}

**GFX12 expert-scheduling exception:** `SIInsertWaitcnts` is not exclusively a memory-wait pass in every mode.

:::

::: {.note}

<strong class="reading-label">Enabled mode</strong>With supported expert scheduling enabled by the option/function-attribute selection, LLVM also tracks VALU VGPR reads/writes and memory-instruction VGPR source reads, and can emit `S_WAITCNT_DEPCTR`.

:::

::: {.note}

<strong class="reading-label">VALU consumers</strong>Its `VA_VDST` waits are cleared before VALU consumers because the source identifies that dependency class as hardware-handled.

:::

::: {.note}

<strong class="reading-label">Dependency fields</strong>These extra dependency fields are separate from the memory-completion counters above and from `fixWMMAHazards`.

:::

::: {.note}

<strong class="reading-label">Sources for this note</strong>[GFX12+ support gate](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/4e9d349ab86dc0a913db3cba11aa2763d6985aff/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/GCNSubtarget.h#L708-L711) · [Enablement](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/4e9d349ab86dc0a913db3cba11aa2763d6985aff/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/AMDGPUWaitcntUtils.cpp#L17-L22) · [Extra events](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/4e9d349ab86dc0a913db3cba11aa2763d6985aff/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/AMDGPUHWEvents.cpp#L23-L57) · [DEPCTR emission](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/4e9d349ab86dc0a913db3cba11aa2763d6985aff/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/SIInsertWaitcnts.cpp#L2346-L2358) · [VALU-consumer exception](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/4e9d349ab86dc0a913db3cba11aa2763d6985aff/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/SIInsertWaitcnts.cpp#L2642-L2649).

:::
